product-scope._note: The PRODUCT's own scope, decomposed ONCE from concept.json and persisted (slice-068 / [[ADR-067]]). Written by /slice-candidates --product via scripts/lib/product_scope.py; NEVER hand-authored by a model. Item ids are minted by the RECEIVER (id_allocator, in-lock): spike B1 measured only 22% cross-run key agreement between two BLIND decompositions of the SAME concept -- 5 of 7 semantically-identical items drifted their key, including the orchestrator itself -- so a model-emitted key can never be a cross-run identity, and a key-match dedup would re-mint 78% of the backlog on every run. depends_on carries PS ids (the model's run-local labels are rewritten inside the lock; decomposition_label keeps the original for traceability). materialize mints one candidate per item, deduped on candidate provenance source:[{type:'product-scope', ref:'PS-NNN'}] across live u archive -- the archive half is load-bearing, or a shipped item is resurrected forever. persist is CREATE-ONLY; revise is the deliberate scope correction (preserves already-minted ids BY id, never re-mints). Every item MUST carry >=1 BLOCKING assumption: /risk-spike step-0 SKIPS a candidate that has none, and a product capability is unproven by definition. That assumption must also still be `unproven` when it is NEW -- but NOT for an item already materialized as a candidate (its spike has necessarily already run), or one proven spike would freeze the scope forever (slice-073 / [[ADR-079]]). `revise` REFUSES a payload that silently omits a live item; the only way to remove one is `revise --cut PS-NNN --reason '<why>'`, which appends to the APPEND-ONLY `revisions[]` ledger below -- prior entries are never rewritten or truncated. `revisions` is OPTIONAL and array-shaped (artifact_lint.OPTIONAL_KEYS): an ABSENT key is a legal, permanent state meaning `empty history`, never a refusal and never a migration -- a membership-preserving revise never creates it. Its `cut` ids are LOAD-BEARING, not documentation: they are the ps retirement history that id_allocator.seed_max_for('ps') scans so a retired PS id is never re-issued onto a shipped candidate. `reason` is required IFF `cut` (an added item is self-describing; a cut destroys the only record of what was there), hence null on the add-only record.

story-sections.title: realtime-presence
story-sections.headline: Show teammates who's viewing a document, live.
story-sections.tldr_md: We're adding a small live indicator so people editing a shared document can see who else is looking at it right now. The first plan needed one always-open connection per viewer; testing showed a single server couldn't hold enough of those, so the design switched to a lighter live feed. A reviewer also caught that the feed didn't check who was asking, so we added a sign-in check before any names are shared.

signoff._note: Optional. Who has actually said 'yes' to this slice, separated by WHAT did the approving: reality (a spike on a real environment, or real-device/data testing) vs the model (a design or code review). Reality-approved and model-approved are NOT the same green. not_yet = checks that haven't happened at this lifecycle stage.

reality_approved.what: Could one server hold 500 always-open live connections? Tested on a real managed server — it tapped out near 120, so the design switched to a lighter one-way feed.

model_approved.what: The plan was reviewed and one real gap — a live feed that didn't check who was asking — was found and fixed before any code was written.

not_yet: Reality testing on real devices and data hasn't happened yet — that comes after the build, when the slice is checked against the real world.

sections.heading: What we set out to do
sections.body_md: When several people open the same document, no one can tell who else is there. This slice adds **live presence**: the avatars of everyone currently viewing a document, appearing and disappearing as they come and go. It's for teams who edit shared docs together and keep stepping on each other's work.

items.label: A teammate's avatar appears within about 2 seconds of them opening the doc.
items.detail: Checked with two real browsers on one document.

sections.heading: What we proved before building
sections.body_md: The original idea was one always-open connection per viewer. Before committing, we ran a quick experiment to see how many of those a single managed server could actually hold.

items.label: Could one server hold 500 live connections? No.
items.detail: It started failing around 120. So we changed course: instead of an always-open socket per viewer, the page now subscribes to a lightweight one-way live feed.

sections.tech_note_md: Dropped raw WebSockets for **server-sent events (SSE)** with reconnect/backoff. A managed pub/sub remains the fallback if SSE fan-out becomes the bottleneck.

sections.heading: How it's built
sections.body_md: A small **presence** service tracks who is currently on each document. The document page subscribes to a live feed when it loads and updates the avatars as people join or leave. Identity comes from the existing sign-in session; if the feed drops, the page quietly reconnects.
sections.tech_note_md: New endpoint `GET /presence/:doc` (SSE) emits `{userId, joined}` events. `presence.ts` owns state; `doc-view` subscribes on mount. Auth via the existing session cookie. No new database tables.

items.label: We committed to a server-sent-events feed here.
items.detail: That's costly to undo later, so we only locked it because this slice needs it.

sections.heading: What the review changed
sections.body_md: An independent review of the plan found one real problem worth fixing before building.

items.label: The live feed didn't check who was asking — anyone could watch a document's viewers.
items.detail: Fixed in the plan: the feed now requires a signed-in session before it opens.

items.label: A second look noted there was no test for the feed dropping and reconnecting.
items.detail: Added to the build's checklist so a dropped connection is exercised.

glossary.plain: a one-way live feed the browser keeps open to receive updates the moment they happen.
